title: MEND: Label-Free Detection, Localisation, and Correction of Latent Hallucination in World Models
abstract: arXiv:2609.39182v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: World Models are appearing as the next major frontier in computer vision. However, their robustness is currently largely unexplored. We identify the phenomenon of hallucination in latent World Models: given a state and an action, the predicted next latent can decode to a scene that never occurs. Because the prediction is statistically ordinary and is fed back autoregressively by the model, the error is both silent and compounding. We study whether such latent hallucination can be detected, localised, and corrected at inference time, on a frozen self-supervised world model in the absence of ground-truth error labels. We introduce Masked Empirical-Bayes Neural Denoising (MEND), a single conditional score network trained by denoising score matching on real transitions, whose score field serves three roles: its magnitude detects hallucination, its per-token field localises it to specific image patches, and it defines an inference-time corr

translated_title: MEND：世界模型中潜在幻觉的无标签检测、定位与修正
translated_abstract: 世界模型正在成为计算机视觉的下一个重大前沿，然而其鲁棒性目前在很大程度上尚未被探索。我们识别出了潜在世界模型中的幻觉现象：给定一个状态和一个动作，模型预测的下一个潜在表示可能解码出一个从未真实发生过的场景。由于该预测在统计上是正常的，且会被模型以自回归方式反馈回去，这种误差既隐蔽又不断累积。我们研究在缺乏真实误差标签的情况下，能否在一个冻结的自监督世界模型上，在推理阶段检测、定位并修正这种潜在幻觉。我们提出了掩码经验贝叶斯神经去噪（MEND），这是一个单一的条件得分网络，通过在真实状态转移数据上进行去噪得分匹配训练得到，其得分场承担三种角色：其幅值可用于检测幻觉，其逐token的得分场可将幻觉定位到具体的图像块，并且它定义了一种推理时的修正机制。
tldr: 该论文提出MEND方法，用一个在真实转移数据上训练的单一条件得分网络，在无需任何误差标签的情况下，于推理阶段对冻结的自监督世界模型的潜在幻觉同时实现检测、定位和修正。
en_tdlr: The paper introduces MEND, a single conditional score network trained by denoising score matching on real transitions, which detects, localises, and corrects latent hallucinations in a frozen self-supervised world model at inference time without any ground-truth error labels.
